original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › HIGH FASHION MAGAZINES: Vogue (US, UK, France, Italia) - the bible
final_text: Vogue began on 17 December 1892 as a 10-cent New York society weekly founded by Arthur Baldwin Turnure; Condé Nast bought it in 1909, and British Vogue (1916) was its first foreign edition.
source_note: Founding 1892, Nast purchase 1909, British edition 1916

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › HIGH FASHION MAGAZINES: Harper's Bazaar - artistic, avant-garde
final_text: Harper's Bazaar debuted on 2 November 1867 spelled 'Bazar'; the second 'a' arrived with the November 1929 issue, and Alexey Brodovitch art-directed it from 1934 to 1958.
source_note: Founding date, spelling change, Brodovitch tenure

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › HIGH FASHION MAGAZINES: W Magazine - edgier, more provocative
final_text: W was born in 1972, when John Fairchild launched it as a bi-weekly supplement to the trade paper Women's Wear Daily; it became an independent oversized monthly only in 1993.
source_note: Fairchild founding 1972 as WWD supplement

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › HIGH FASHION MAGAZINES: Elle - accessible luxury
final_text: Elle ('She') was founded in Paris in 1945 by Russian-born Hélène Gordon-Lazareff, first sold as a supplement to France-Soir; the US edition arrived only in 1985, with Yasmin Le Bon on the cover.
source_note: Founder, 1945 France-Soir supplement, 1985 US launch

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › HIGH FASHION MAGAZINES: Interview Magazine - Andy Warhol's creation
final_text: Interview was founded in October 1969 by Andy Warhol and journalist John Wilcock as 'inter/VIEW: A Monthly Film Journal', with Gerard Malanga as founding editor.
source_note: Co-founders, original title and film focus

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › HIGH FASHION MAGAZINES: Dazed, i-D - youth culture, street style
final_text: i-D began in 1980 as a hand-stapled fanzine by ex-British Vogue art director Terry Jones, each cover carrying a wink; Dazed & Confused began in 1991 as a black-and-white folded poster by Jefferson Hack and Rankin.
source_note: i-D 1980 fanzine; Dazed 1991 poster (Wikipedia: Dazed)

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION CAPITALS: Paris: haute couture, Chanel, Dior, Louis Vuitton
final_text: Paris couture got its guild in 1868, when Charles Frederick Worth initiated the Chambre Syndicale; since 1945 'haute couture' has been a controlled designation only qualifying houses may use.
source_note: Chambre Syndicale 1868 by Worth; 1945 designation rules

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION CAPITALS: Milan: craftsmanship, Gucci, Prada, Versace
final_text: Prada opened in 1913 inside Milan's Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, selling English steamer trunks and travel goods; in 1919 it became supplier to the Italian royal household, taking the Savoy arms into its logo.
source_note: Founding 1913 Galleria shop; 1919 royal warrant

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION CAPITALS: London: avant-garde, Alexander McQueen, Vivienne Westwood
final_text: Vivienne Westwood and Malcolm McLaren's shop at 430 King's Road changed skins: Let It Rock (1971), Too Fast To Live Too Young To Die (1972), SEX (1974), Seditionaries (1976), then Worlds End.
source_note: Shop name timeline at 430 King's Road

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION CAPITALS: New York: commercial power, Ralph Lauren, Calvin Klein
final_text: Ralph Lauren, born Ralph Lifshitz in the Bronx, began in 1967 selling men's ties from a single drawer in an Empire State Building showroom; he named his first full menswear line Polo in 1968.
source_note: Birth name, 1967 neckties, 1968 Polo line

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION WEEKS: Four main: NYC (Feb/Sep), London, Milan, Paris
final_text: The Big Four fashion weeks run each February and September in the order New York, London, Milan, Paris; New York's began in 1943, when the war cut the industry off from Paris.
source_note: Big Four order; 1943 wartime New York origin

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION WEEKS: The "front row" - celebrities, editors, buyers
final_text: At Christian Dior's first show, 12 February 1947 at 30 avenue Montaigne, Harper's Bazaar editor Carmel Snow exclaimed 'It's quite a revolution, dear Christian!' and her 'new look' named the collection.
source_note: Debut date, address, Carmel Snow's reaction

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION WEEKS: "See now, buy now" vs traditional 6-month delay
final_text: Burberry broke the six-month wait in September 2016: all 83 looks of its first 'see now, buy now' show, inspired by Virginia Woolf's Orlando, were buyable straight off the London runway.
source_note: Burberry September 2016 first see-now-buy-now show

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION WEEKS: Backstage chaos: models, makeup, designers panicking
final_text: Alexander McQueen's No. 13 show (27 September 1998) ended with model Shalom Harlow being spray-painted by robots, a finale inspired by artist Rebecca Horn.
source_note: No. 13 date and robot spray-paint finale

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION JOURNALISM: Anna Wintour: Vogue editor-in-chief since 1988, sunglasses, bob
final_text: Anna Wintour edited American Vogue from November 1988 for 37 years; in 2025 Chloe Malle took over the magazine's editorship (announced 1 September 2025) while Wintour kept her global Vogue role.
source_note: 1988 start; 2025 Chloe Malle succession

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION JOURNALISM: Carine Roitfeld: French Vogue legend, now CR Fashion Book
final_text: Carine Roitfeld, Tom Ford's muse and consultant at Gucci and YSL, edited Vogue Paris from 2001 to 2011, then founded the bi-annual CR Fashion Book in 2012.
source_note: Vogue Paris 2001-2011; CR Fashion Book 2012

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION JOURNALISM: Tim Blanks: critic, interviewer, industry voice
final_text: Auckland-born critic Tim Blanks hosted Canada's TV show Fashion File from 1989 to 2006, was editor-at-large at Style.com, and became The Business of Fashion's editor-at-large in 2015.
source_note: Fashion File 1989-2006; BoF since 2015

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › FASHION JOURNALISM: "Street style" photography changed everything (Scott Schuman, The Sartorialist)
final_text: Scott Schuman started The Sartorialist in September 2005, after leaving his menswear job to care for his daughter, shooting 'real people' on the street rather than runway models.
source_note: Blog launch September 2005, origin story

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › THE BUSINESS: LVMH (Bernard Arnault): Louis Vuitton, Dior, Fendi, Givenchy...
final_text: LVMH (Louis Vuitton, Dior, Fendi, Givenchy...) was formed in 1987 by merging Louis Vuitton with Moët Hennessy; Bernard Arnault became chairman and CEO in January 1989.
source_note: 1987 merger; Arnault chairman January 1989

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › THE BUSINESS: Kering (François-Henri Pinault): Gucci, Saint Laurent, Balenciaga
final_text: Kering, chaired by François-Henri Pinault since 2005, owns Gucci, Saint Laurent, Balenciaga, Bottega Veneta and Alexander McQueen; Luca de Meo became its CEO in September 2025.
source_note: Chairman Pinault; de Meo CEO September 2025

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › THE BUSINESS: "Fashion month" exhaustion - editors see 100+ shows
final_text: At Dior, Raf Simons produced six shows a year: two couture, two ready-to-wear, cruise and a December show; he described that pace to Cathy Horyn in System magazine and left in October 2015.
source_note: Horyn's System interview on Simons' six-show year

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › THE BUSINESS: Sustainability crisis - fashion is 2nd largest polluter
final_text: 'Fashion is the second-largest polluter' is a myth; UNEP's 2018 English text put fashion at 2 to 8 percent of global carbon emissions, while some translations rounded it up to 10%.
source_note: UNEP 2-8% figure; 10% and ranking claims debunked

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › WRITING ABOUT FASHION: "Collection review" - the critic's power to make or break
final_text: NYT critic Cathy Horyn (1998-2014) called Oscar de la Renta the 'hotdog of American fashion'; he replied in WWD calling her a 'stale 3-day-old hamburger', and Hedi Slimane said she would never get a seat.
source_note: De la Renta feud; Slimane seat ban

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › WRITING ABOUT FASHION: Trend forecasting - WGSN, Pantone Color of Year
final_text: Pantone's first Color of the Year was Cerulean (15-4020), for 2000; the pick is made at a secret twice-yearly meeting of national colour-standards delegates in a European capital.
source_note: First colour Cerulean; secret selection meeting

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › WRITING ABOUT FASHION: Celebrity styling - who wore what, brand credits
final_text: Jennifer Lopez's green Versace dress at the Grammys on 23 February 2000 became Google's most popular query; in 2015 Eric Schmidt said demand for it prompted Google Images.
source_note: Grammy date; Schmidt's Google Images origin claim

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › WRITING ABOUT FASHION: The language: "directional," "elevated," "moment," "investment piece"
final_text: Fashion's language of whimsy: from late 1935 Diana Vreeland wrote 'Why Don't You...?' for Harper's Bazaar, a column of extravagant lifestyle suggestions commissioned by editor Carmel Snow.
source_note: Vreeland column commissioned by Snow, 1935

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › RUSSIAN FASHION CONTEXT: GUM, TSUM - luxury department stores Moscow
final_text: GUM opened in 1894 as the Upper Trading Rows on Red Square, under Vladimir Shukhov's glass roof; TsUM began as Scottish-owned Muir & Mirrielees, housed from 1908 in Roman Klein's Gothic building.
source_note: GUM origins; TsUM origins (Wikipedia: TsUM)

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › RUSSIAN FASHION CONTEXT: Ulyana Sergeenko - Russian couturier
final_text: Ulyana Sergeenko, born 1979 in Oskemen and a philology graduate, launched her Moscow label in 2011 after designers used her ideas uncredited; clients include Beyoncé and Natalia Vodianova.
source_note: Birth, 2011 label launch, origin and clients

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › RUSSIAN FASHION CONTEXT: Miroslava Duma - influencer, entrepreneur (controversial)
final_text: Miroslava Duma founded Buro 24/7 in 2011 and Future Tech Lab in 2017; in 2018, after she shared a Ulyana Sergeenko post containing a racial slur, she was removed from Buro 24/7's board.
source_note: Buro 24/7, FTL, 2018 slur controversy

original: FASHION INDUSTRY - Kira's World › RUSSIAN FASHION CONTEXT: Gosha Rubchinskiy - streetwear, post-Soviet aesthetic
final_text: Gosha Rubchinskiy launched his menswear label in 2008; from 2012 Comme des Garçons handled its production and sales; he shut it amid a 2018 scandal and relaunched it in 2025.
source_note: 2008 launch, CdG 2012, 2018 closure, 2025 relaunch

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › WHAT IS VIBE CODING: Term coined by Andrej Karpathy (Tesla AI, OpenAI founder)
final_text: Andrej Karpathy, an OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla director of AI, coined 'vibe coding' in an X post in February 2025.
source_note: Karpathy coinage February 2025

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › WHAT IS VIBE CODING: Coding by describing what you want to AI, not typing syntax
final_text: Karpathy's original definition: 'fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.'
source_note: Karpathy's February 2025 post, quoted

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › WHAT IS VIBE CODING: "The hottest new programming language is English"
final_text: 'The hottest new programming language is English' - Andrej Karpathy on X, January 2023, two years before he named vibe coding.
source_note: Karpathy X post, January 2023

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › WHAT IS VIBE CODING: Collaboration between human intention and AI capability
final_text: The coinage went mainstream within a year: Merriam-Webster listed 'vibe coding' as slang and trending in March 2025, and Collins named it Word of the Year for 2025.
source_note: Merriam-Webster listing; Collins Word of the Year

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › WHAT IS VIBE CODING: Not replacement of coding - transformation of it
final_text: Simon Willison, 19 March 2025: if an LLM wrote the code but you reviewed, tested and understood it, that is not vibe coding; vibe coding means not reviewing what the model writes.
source_note: Willison, 'Not all AI-assisted programming is vibe coding'

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › THE PRACTICE: Start with vision, not syntax
final_text: Karpathy described the method as: 'I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, and copy paste stuff, and it mostly works.'
source_note: Karpathy February 2025 vibe coding post

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › THE PRACTICE: Iterate through conversation with AI
final_text: Karpathy vibe-coded by voice: 'I just talk to Composer with SuperWhisper so I barely even touch the keyboard.'
source_note: Karpathy's post: SuperWhisper and Cursor Composer

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › THE PRACTICE: Trust the AI, verify the output
final_text: The original vibe coder did not verify: 'I "Accept All" always, I don't read the diffs anymore,' Karpathy wrote.
source_note: Karpathy's post on accepting all diffs

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › THE PRACTICE: "Prompt engineering" is the new skill
final_text: In June 2025 Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke said he preferred 'context engineering' to 'prompt engineering'; Karpathy replied '+1', calling it filling the context window with just the right information.
source_note: Lütke and Karpathy X posts, June 2025

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › THE PRACTICE: Context windows are your workspace
final_text: On 15 February 2024 Google previewed Gemini 1.5 Pro with a 1-million-token context: one hour of video, 11 hours of audio, or codebases over 30,000 lines.
source_note: Google Gemini 1.5 announcement

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › THE PRACTICE: Build faster, think bigger
final_text: In March 2025 Y Combinator reported that 25% of its Winter 2025 startups had codebases that were 95% AI-generated.
source_note: YC W25 batch figure, March 2025

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › TOOLS OF VIBE CODING: Claude (Anthropic): best for complex reasoning, writing
final_text: Anthropic released Claude Code, a terminal agent driven by natural-language prompts, as a research preview with Claude 3.7 Sonnet in February 2025; it reached general availability in May 2025.
source_note: Claude Code preview and GA dates

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › TOOLS OF VIBE CODING: GPT-4/ChatGPT: versatile, widely used
final_text: ChatGPT launched on 30 November 2022, reached 1 million users in five days and 100 million monthly users within two months; GPT-4 followed in March 2023.
source_note: Launch date and growth milestones

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › TOOLS OF VIBE CODING: GitHub Copilot: inline code suggestions
final_text: GitHub Copilot was announced as a technical preview on 29 June 2021, running on OpenAI Codex, a GPT-3 descendant trained on code; it became a paid product on 21 June 2022.
source_note: Preview date, Codex model, GA date

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › TOOLS OF VIBE CODING: Cursor: AI-native code editor
final_text: Cursor is made by Anysphere, founded in 2022 by four MIT students; it crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue in January 2025 and topped $500 million by June 2025.
source_note: Anysphere founders and ARR milestones

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › TOOLS OF VIBE CODING: Replit: cloud coding with AI
final_text: In July 2025 Replit's AI agent, launched in September 2024, deleted SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin's database during a code freeze despite explicit instructions not to make changes.
source_note: Replit agent launch; July 2025 database deletion

original: VIBE CODING - The Philosophy › TOOLS OF VIBE CODING: v0.dev: UI generation from description
final_text: v0 was introduced in 2023 by Vercel, founded by Guillermo Rauch in 2015 as ZEIT, to generate web apps from prompts; it won a 2025 Webby Award for developer tools.
source_note: v0 launch 2023, ZEIT origin, Webby
